summary: McChord Air Force Base (IATA: TCM, ICAO: KTCM) is a U.S. Air Force installation in Tacoma, Washington, and part of Joint Base Lewis-McChord. It is home to the 62nd Airlift Wing and its C-17 Globemaster III fleet, supporting global military airlift and cargo missions. The airfield is an active military facility and does not offer scheduled commercial passenger service.
faqs:
Q: Is McChord Air Force Base open to the public?
A: No, it is an active military installation; access is restricted to authorized personnel, dependents, retirees, and visitors with valid passes or escorts.

Q: Does TCM offer commercial passenger flights?
A: No, there is no scheduled commercial airline service; the airfield primarily supports military airlift, cargo, and Space-Available military flights.

Q: What aircraft are based at McChord?
A: The 62nd Airlift Wing operates C-17 Globemaster III aircraft, and other military units may transit through the field.

Q: How do I get a visitor pass for McChord Field?
A: Visitors generally need to be sponsored by an authorized ID card holder and process through Joint Base Lewis-McChord visitor control at designated gates; requirements can change, so check current JBLM access procedures.
transport_tips: Access to McChord Field is through Joint Base Lewis-McChord gates, usually from I-5 exits 119 or 120, and requires a valid military ID or approved visitor pass. There is no scheduled public transit or commercial airline service at the airfield, so driving or rideshare to an authorized gate is the practical option. Allow extra time for gate security checks, especially during weekday commute hours.
local_tip: For eligible travelers, the McChord Passenger Terminal handles Space-Available military flights; check roll-call times and bring leave or authorization paperwork, as schedules can change with little notice.
